html:
A magnitude 9.0 to 9.1 undersea earthquake off northeastern Japan on 11 March 2011, the strongest ever recorded in Japan, and the tsunami it raised. Waves up to about 40 m high swept over the Tōhoku coast within an hour. About 18,000 people died or are still missing, most of them drowned.

The tsunami also knocked out power and cooling at the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant. Three reactors melted down and well over 100,000 people were evacuated. The Fukushima disaster was the worst nuclear accident since Chernobyl in 1986. Japan shut down its reactors for years, and Germany decided to close all of its own.

Japan's strict building codes kept most buildings standing through the shaking; the sea did most of the killing. The quake moved part of Honshu a few metres east. It came seven years after the Indian Ocean tsunami of 2004, and it renewed worldwide work on tsunami warnings and sea walls.
